text:
maya: Heads-up — spotted a weird p95 bump in small-batch decode on nightly after the flash-paged kernel flip. Looks like prefill is fine but decode tail latency spikes when batch size==1 and kv cache hit ratio drops.

arjun: Can you paste the perf trace / kernel selection log?

maya: Sure. Short summary: decode requests end up hitting FlashVariantB (paged+fusion) for step kernels, but we see frequent kernel re-launches and a lot of memcopy churn. p95 +12% vs yesterday.

maya: Perf snippet:
```
kernel_select: FlashVariantB (paged-fused) -> launch_time 1.8ms
kernel_relaunch: 0.9ms (avg)
kv_cache_hit: 72% overall, but 42% for small-batch decode
decode_step_time: median 3.2ms, p95 8.9ms (yesterday p95 7.9ms)
```

perf-bot: Regression alert: decode p95 increased by 12% on nightly (job: nightly-small-decode-bench). Trace ID: trace_2026_03_17_09_12. :warning:

sasha: Interesting — the kv cache hit drop for small-batch smells like fragmentation across kv pages when sequence length distribution gets wide. Any recent changes to kvpage allocator or stride selection?

maya: We rolled the paged allocator tweak in #3442 (kvpage coalescing) two days ago. The change reduced memory pressure but might have widened page boundaries.

arjun: Could also be warmup heuristics: continuous batching disabled for decode path in the same release? If decode stops queuing and goes immediate for batch==1, we lose beneficial coalescing.

maya: Right — decode continuous-batching flag was flipped for a short trial. That lines up with when p95 moved. But the kernel log shows a lot of FlashVariantB launches vs FlashVariantA (fused non-paged) which used to be chosen for small seqs. The selector seems more aggressive toward paged-fused now.

taylor: Quick mitigation: toggle selector to prefer non-paged fused kernel for decode when batch_size<=2 and seq<=64. Also bump kvpage eviction threshold to avoid grabbing cold pages. Can we test a canary with that override?

maya: Trying a canary now on canary-14. Run command to reproduce locally:
```bash
PYENV=venv-dev ./bench_decode --model redwood-7b --batch 1 --seq 32 --kv-cache --iters 500 --trace-kernel-select > out.log
```

sasha: Ping me when you have the canary trace. I want to look at the memcopy vs kernel_compute split in the flamegraph.

perf-bot: Canary started: canary-14 using selector-override preferring FlashVariantA for small decode. Baseline job: nightly-small-decode-bench.

maya: Canary trace: kernel_relaunchs dropped from 0.9ms -> 0.12ms, kv_cache_hit for small decode rose to 88%, p95 back to 7.8ms. So selector change looks promising.

arjun: Nice. Need to validate across varying seq distributions — some customers have long prefill and tiny decode, which interacts with kv page fragmentation. Also check memory usage (coalescing revert might raise resident slightly).

taylor: I'll open a short-lived feature flag with metric dashboards: decode_p95, kv_hit_rate_by_batch, mem_copy_ratio. Roll to 10% first.

infra-bot: Rollout scheduled: selector-override -> featureflag decode_kern_pref_small -> 10% at 2026-03-17T12:05Z.

maya: Follow-ups: 1) add unit test reproducing kv page fragmentation pattern (vary seq lengths, interleaved prefill/decode), 2) add metric to kernel selector that records why a variant was chosen (cost_model score), 3) consider making continuous-batching opt-in for decode until selector is robust.

sasha: I'll prototype an offline allocator sim that simulates page fragmentation and kv reuse to tune eviction heuristics.

arjun: Also we should add a lightweight perf counter for memcopy bytes per token in decode path — that's the easiest signal to alert on automatically.

maya: Agreed. Thanks all — tracking in the perf board, will post a short summary after the 10% canary completes. :thumbsup:
